criteria.no: The statement adds or changes a substantive policy, mechanism, strength, or outcome.
criteria.unclear: The quote's substantive directive is genuinely ambiguous.
criteria.yes: Every substantive requirement follows from the quote; formal must-language and atomic extraction add no new meaning.

faithful-r2-a-plain-directive.instructions: Does anchor.quote, read as an ordinary user directive even when it says should, needs, or asks informally, support every substantive requirement in anchor.statement? The statement may formalize wording and isolate one directive from a longer quote, but may not invent a policy or mechanism.

criteria.no: Yes; the statement selects an unsupported mechanism, policy, strength, or different outcome.
criteria.unclear: The quote is too ambiguous to tell whether a new decision was introduced.
criteria.yes: No new decision is required; the statement is a faithful formalization of a supported directive.

faithful-r2-b-no-new-decision.instructions: Would adopting anchor.statement require any product or implementation decision beyond anchor.quote's plain directive? Ignore grammatical strength differences between informal user speech and a formal requirement, and ignore unrelated directives in the same quote.

criteria.no: A substantive action, outcome, condition, or prohibition differs or lacks quote support.
criteria.unclear: The quote does not settle the substantive action or outcome.
criteria.yes: The same substantive action and outcome are required or forbidden.

faithful-r2-c-substantive-match.instructions: Compare the substantive action and outcome in anchor.statement with anchor.quote. Do they match, allowing paraphrase, formal must wording, and one atomic anchor per quoted directive?
